english.html: point of this case, the witnesses who so obstinately assured that the accused was Martin Guerre have since recognised their error, and have departed from it before the Court, as will hereafter be said.

notes.citation: Panormitanus (Niccolò de' Tudeschi, Panorme) and the others on c. Praeterea (X 2.20), cited above at {e}
notes.original: Panorme & les autre au c. præterea allegué.
notes.gloss: The just causes for which a witness may be re-examined and may amend what he has said.

english.html: One might here raise some difficulty, and think that one ought not to give great faith to the last deposition of these witnesses, who depart from the first: both because they have varied <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, and thus, by the contradiction and repugnance of their depositions, themselves overthrow it <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>; and because also they are perjured, and the testimony of a perjurer, as everyone understands, ought to be rejected <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>; especially since, if any faith could be given to one of their depositions, it would have to be to the first, made with oath <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>. But all these difficulties can easily be resolved if one comes to consider that it is very reasonable that a witness who, through error and the circumvention of another, has deposed falsely should, as soon as his error appears to him, correct himself <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>: and thus not only on the spot, or shortly after (as is indubitably permitted him <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>), but even after a long space and interval of time, if until then he had not perceived his error, or else some other just cause newly presents itself <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. The judgment of which, together with the distance of time, is wholly referred to the discretion of the judge <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>. Otherwise, if the witness, for his pleasure and of his own free will, long after his deposition wished to depart from it, and to change or correct what he had already deposed, he would not be received to do so, for fear of subornation <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>.

notes.citation: Digest 22.5 (De testibus), l. 2 (D. 22.5.2, Modestinus) and l. Qui falso (D. 22.5.16, Paul); Code 9.22 (Ad legem Corneliam de falsis), l. Eos (fragment not identified)
notes.original: l. ij l. qui falſo. D. de te ſtib. l. eos. C. de falſ.
notes.gloss: D. 22.5.2: witnesses who waver against the faith of their own testimony are not to be heard; D. 22.5.16: those who have given false or varying testimony, or betrayed both parties, are punished by the judges.
